messages:
jamie: Customer hit a reproducible case where a structured (JSON mode) SSE stream is cut mid-object when a kvcache_prefix is used and Cloudflare is in front. They get a perfectly well-formed start, then the connection closes and client-side JSON parsing fails. stack: node -> CF -> our hosted API.

alice: Can you paste the exact curl they used + the partial response body? Also what model and schema were they using?

jamie: From customer: 
```bash
curl -v -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses/stream -d '{"mode":"structured","model":"rwd-instruct-4x","input":"...","kvcache_prefix":"customer_abc"}'
```
Partial stream received (literal SSE lines):
```
data: {"role":"assistant","content":{"type":"json","value":{"items":[{"id":1,"text":"hello"},{"id":2,"text":"world"},
```
then EOF — trailing `]}}` never arrives and client throws a parse error.

tom_customer: Confirmed. Only happens when `kvcache_prefix` is present and the request goes through CF. If I remove prefix or call directly to the origin, the stream completes. Frequency ~5-10%.

ravi: Do CF logs show any 5xx? Any `Connection: close` on their side? Could be keepalive timeouts or CF buffering logic closing an idle connection after a burst from cache. Also check our ingress timeouts and whether we set a premature Content-Length.

jamie: They attached CF edge logs showing a `502` at the time the client saw EOF. Our upstream host logs show the connection reset by peer — we don't have an application error recorded.

maria: Hypothesis: when we interleave cached SSE events (immediate) followed by live generation, CF might decide the early cached burst is complete and subsequently terminate the TCP connection when it sees a quick pause. Another possibility: our SSE framing currently can split JSON objects across events; if an intermediate event is lost/trimmed by a proxy, the final concatenation is invalid.

alice: Can we reproduce locally with an nginx/CF-like proxy in front and kvcache enabled? If it only repros with CF behavior, ask customer for tcpdump + timing. If repros without CF, it's our bug.

maria: I ran a quick repro with staging + nginx ingress. I implemented a small server that writes a cached SSE event, then streams the rest token-by-token and intentionally closed the socket after the second event. Client saw identical truncated JSON. That shows our code path can emit a premature close if some code path calls `res.end()` early.

ravi: Action items for eng-runtime: 1) Audit the code path that stitches cached SSE events with live generators. Ensure we never call `res.end()` until the generator Promise resolves or times out. 2) Add an explicit final SSE event like `data: {"__stream_complete":true}` to mark a clean EOF for structured mode. 3) Confirm we never send `Content-Length` for streaming responses and that Transfer-Encoding: chunked is used. 4) Add instrumentation: emit a debug event when a stream ends without the stream-complete marker.

jamie: Customer says billing registered tokens for partial stream; they're asking for a credit if we confirm the cut happened server-side. Their app counts objects and fails on parse error, so tokens are charged but response was unusable.

alice: I'll coordinate with support ops on a goodwill credit if we verify. Meanwhile, Ravi/Maria, can you prepare a minimal patch and an internal staging test that simulates cached-prefix + proxy edge and checks for finalization marker? Post ETA here.

ravi: ETA for patch: 48h to land guard against early `res.end()` + add finalization event. ETA for staging test: 24h. I'll push a draft PR and link it.

maria: Also propose short-term workaround: disable kvcache_prefix for customers behind CF until patch is validated. I'll draft a support note with steps.

alice: Thanks. @tom_customer we'll follow up with a timeline and ask for tcpdump if problem persists after patch. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy started staging/edge-repro-test -> staging (runtimes v2.14.1-hotfix)

jamie: I'll keep the customer updated. Will attach their curl + timestamps once they send tcpdump.
